h1: Milvus vs Weaviate: an open-source vector database comparison
intro: Milvus and Weaviate differ in architecture and operating model. Milvus persists data in object storage and scales query, ingest and indexing resources separately. Weaviate manages collection shards and replicas on its nodes, with vectorizer modules, GraphQL and native multi-tenancy. Both integrate with embedding providers and offer multiple index and compression choices. Choose by workload, existing APIs and operating experience.

sections.h2: Milvus vs Weaviate scalability: how does each grow to billions of vectors?
paragraphs: Milvus is built on storage compute separation. Segments and the write-ahead log live in object storage, so a new query node loads its assigned segments instead of copying another node's disk, and ingestion, search and indexing each scale on separate node types. Tiered storage lets a node serve more data than fits in its memory and disk.

Weaviate splits collections into shards, with objects and indexes on node-local storage. Plan collection sharding ahead; MOVE/COPY APIs relocate or copy existing replicas after adding nodes. Capacity depends on the chosen index: HNSW memory depends on its vector cache and quantization, while HFresh provides a disk-backed path. One RAM multiplier does not describe all configurations.

sections.h2: Weaviate vs Milvus features: a vector database comparison table
paragraphs: Both engines cover dense, sparse and hybrid retrieval with metadata filtering. Weaviate's distinctive strengths are model integrations and native multi-tenancy; Milvus offers more index families across memory, disk and GPU, plus server-side BM25. Readers weighing Milvus vs Weaviate vs Qdrant for the best open source vector database can pair this table with our Qdrant comparison.

Does Milvus or Weaviate integrate better with LangChain or LlamaIndex? Both ship first-party LangChain, LlamaIndex and Haystack integrations, so the RAG framework rarely decides it; Dify defaults to Weaviate and also supports Milvus.

sections.h2: Milvus vs Weaviate cost and operations: what does each take to run?
paragraphs: Evaluate compute, RAM, storage, networking and operations together. Weaviate offers different tradeoffs through HNSW, quantization, HFresh and tenant offloading; Milvus offers quantized HNSW, DiskANN and tiered storage. Compare at matching recall and latency targets rather than estimating from raw vector size alone. Neither requires Kubernetes to start.

sections.h2: When is Weaviate the better choice?
paragraphs: Choose by workload and operating model. Weaviate offers model integrations, native multi-tenancy and GraphQL; Milvus separates query, ingest and indexing resources. Compare recall, latency, throughput and operations on your own data rather than treating a corpus size as a hard product boundary.
bullets: You want built-in vectorizer, generative and reranker modules instead of an embedding pipeline.
Your application already speaks GraphQL, or you prefer Weaviate's object-centric data model.
Data fits a small cluster whose shard count and replication factor you can size up front.
Thousands of small tenants, each as its own shard, with cold tenants offloaded to S3.
You run Weaviate Cloud and want serverless pricing with the same client API.

faqs: Weaviate vs Milvus: which should I use?

Milvus and Weaviate differ in architecture and operating model. Milvus persists data in object storage and scales query, ingest and indexing resources separately. Weaviate manages collection shards and replicas on its nodes, with vectorizer modules, GraphQL and native multi-tenancy. Both integrate with embedding providers and offer multiple index and compression choices. Choose by workload, existing APIs and operating experience.
Which is faster, Milvus or Weaviate?

These charts show the verified Milvus and Zilliz Cloud VectorDBBench configurations. They do not include a same-condition result for the other product, so they cannot establish a speed advantage. Benchmark with matching data, filters, recall targets and hardware before comparing.
Which scales better, Weaviate or Milvus?

Weaviate splits collections into shards, with objects and indexes on node-local storage. Plan collection sharding ahead; MOVE/COPY APIs relocate or copy existing replicas after adding nodes. Capacity depends on the chosen index: HNSW memory depends on its vector cache and quantization, while HFresh provides a disk-backed path. One RAM multiplier does not describe all configurations.

Yes. The Weaviate open source license is BSD-3-Clause for the core repository, with a separate commercially licensed wl/ directory. Milvus is Apache-2.0 and an LF AI & Data graduated project. Both can be self-hosted, and each has a managed service: Weaviate Cloud and Zilliz Cloud.

Yes. Weaviate hybrid search combines a BM25F keyword query with a vector query, weighted by alpha and fused with relativeScoreFusion or rankedFusion. Milvus runs hybrid search across several vector fields, including BM25 sparse vectors generated on the server, fused with RRF or a weighted ranker.
Can I run Milvus without Kubernetes in production?

Yes. Milvus Standalone packs every component into a single Docker image with the Woodpecker WAL embedded and is documented up to 100 million vectors; Milvus Lite is a Python library for a few million. Kubernetes, via Helm or the Milvus Operator, is for Milvus Distributed.
Is switching from Weaviate to Milvus a drop-in migration?

No. A Weaviate collection maps to a Milvus collection with scalar fields, and named vectors to multiple vector fields. Export objects with their vectors, bulk-insert into Milvus, build indexes, and rewrite hybrid queries from alpha fusion to RRF or a weighted ranker.
What is the difference between Milvus and Zilliz Cloud?
Zilliz Cloud is fully managed Milvus from the team that created it. It uses the same client APIs, so code written against Milvus Lite or Standalone moves to Zilliz Cloud without a rewrite.
